Class TrustedChaosEnablement

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.spring.boot.common.TrustedChaosEnablement
public final class TrustedChaosEnablement extends Object
Decides whether macstab.chaos.enabled=true may switch chaos on, based on which property source the value came from.

Attaching a JVM agent is a launch-time decision. The flag is honoured only when the property source that wins for macstab.chaos.enabled is a local, launch-time source:

  • JVM system properties, environment variables, command-line arguments and SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON;
  • config data bundled on the classpath (application.properties / .yml, including profile-specific variants), read from a local file ( ./config/application.yml, spring.config.location=file:…) or from a config tree (Kubernetes ConfigMap and Secret mounts, configtree:);
  • property sources created by Spring's test support (@SpringBootTest(properties), @TestPropertySource(properties), @DynamicPropertySource, TestPropertyValues), which exist only in test contexts.

Every other source — Spring Cloud Config, Consul, Vault, any remote or runtime override — is ignored: honouring it would turn a compromised config server into the ability to instrument the JVM. Operators who need remote enablement opt in by setting macstab.chaos.allow-remote-enable=true through a trusted source, which is itself subject to the same check.

Booleans are read as Spring binds them: true|false|1|0|yes|no|on|off; any other value is off, with one warning.

The same decision gates both the early self-attach in the version-specific EnvironmentPostProcessor and ChaosAutoConfiguration. Gating only the former would let the auto-configuration attach the agent anyway from an untrusted source.
